literal: Having been intoxicated I know not, saying that let one abandon; in the heart even that which was hidden right there will increase.
translation: Let one give up saying, "I have never known intoxication." When drunk, even the secrets hidden deep in the heart will readily reveal themselves.
modern: நான் குடித்து அறியமாட்டேன் என்று சொல்வதைக் கைவிட வேண்டும். குடித்தால், மனத்திற்குள் மறைத்து வைத்திருந்த ரகசியங்களும் அப்போதே வெளிப்பட்டுவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the self-deception of a drinker who claims they have never been intoxicated. The word 'kaḷittu' specifically means being intoxicated by drink in this chapter's context. The poet points out that alcohol strips away inhibitions, so 'oḷittatūum' (even hidden things) in the mind will 'mikum' (increase or become manifest) right then and there. Thus, trying to hide one's drinking is futile, as the drink itself will force the truth out.
